Okay so right now I'm at Foothill Peaks Medical Center here in Denver. I'm part-time, which honestly I never thought I'd say, I was always the one picking up extra shifts. I'm 0.6, so two twelves a week, 24 hours, mostly in the ICU. It's a mixed medical-surgical ICU, and sometimes they float me to step-down when they're short, which is a lot.

How I got here. We moved up from San Antonio in March 2022 because Daniel, my partner, got a job offer here, he's a civil engineer, and it was too good for him to pass up. I'd been off work for a while at that point, after the travel nursing stuff, so the timing kind of worked out. I didn't actually start at Foothill Peaks until July 2022 because the license transfer took forever. Well, Texas and Colorado are both compact states so it shouldn't have, but there was some issue with my address change and the background check. Anyway. July 2022.

The part-time thing was on purpose. I knew I didn't want to go back to full-time bedside. I love my patients, I do, but my back, and also I think after COVID I just can't do three or four twelves a week anymore and still be a person. So I took part-time and kept the other days for figuring out what's next.

The thing I'm proudest of here honestly isn't even the nursing part. When I started, our unit's staffing was done on a paper grid and a whiteboard, and the charge nurse would be texting people at four in the morning trying to fill holes. I built a Google Sheet, a staffing grid, where the charge enters census and acuity, and it shows where we're going to be short over the next 24 hours and color codes it, red, yellow, green. My manager liked it and now she pulls it up every morning for our unit huddle. I think it saves her like an hour a day? She said that once, I didn't time it. I'd honestly say my sheet is basically how the hospital does staffing now. Which, okay, it's mostly our unit. A couple of other managers asked for a copy, but I don't know if they actually use it.

The other big thing was the virtual nursing pilot in 2024. The hospital was trying out having a nurse work remotely, from a little office with a camera and a screen in the patient rooms, doing admissions, discharge teaching, med reconciliation, all the documentation stuff, so the bedside nurses could actually be at the bedside. They picked six of us bedside nurses to pilot it and I was one of them. It was for a 28-bed med-surg unit, not my ICU. I did it for about four months, so two of my shifts a week were virtual instead of ICU. I really liked it. I liked figuring out the workflow, like what the virtual nurse owns and what the bedside nurse owns, who signs what, and we kept a shared doc of everything that was breaking. I think I wrote most of that doc, honestly. Discharge teaching got way more consistent, the bedside nurses said they had more time, and I think the discharges-before-noon number went up but I never saw the final report. The pilot ended when the grant money ran out, or that's what we were told, I'm not totally sure. They said they'd revisit it in 2026 and so far, no.

That pilot is what made me look at the operations side of healthcare. I realized I like the part where you figure out how the work should flow more than I like doing the twelfth bath of the night. Sorry, that sounds bad. You know what I mean.

So last September, September 2025, I started the Google Data Analytics certificate. Spreadsheets, SQL, a bit of R which I did not love, Tableau, and I ended up doing my capstone in Looker Studio because it was free and easy to share. I finished in June 2026. For the capstone I did a staffing ratio dashboard, nurse-to-patient ratios by shift against census and acuity, on made-up data, because obviously I can't use real patient stuff. It's on my GitHub. It's not fancy, but I actually understand what a join is now, which a year ago, no way.

Oh, and I'm on the unit practice council here, we meet once a month, I've been on it since 2023. We redid how we do bedside shift report, that was most of last year. That's about it for here, I think.
